subtopics.title: Can the Bills Be Paid? — the Liquidity Ratios

questions.question: The current ratio for Zanele's Trading is:
options: 44 400 : 11 100 — exactly 4 : 1: four rand turning to cash for every rand knocking

questions.question: The acid-test ratio removes inventories because:
options: Stock must still find a buyer, at a decent price, in time — it is the least cash-like current asset
The formula only fits three figures

questions.question: The guideline norms for the two liquidity ratios are:
options: Roughly 2 : 1 (current) and 1 : 1 (acid test) — held as GUIDES, never laws
No norms exist at Grade 10 level

questions.question: A very high current ratio can be criticised because:
options: It proves the business is insolvent
High ratios always mean the books are wrong
It shows the bills cannot be paid
Excess liquidity is idle money — R24 500 dozing in the bank instead of earning the mark-up or settling the 10% loan

questions.question: The solvency ratio is:
The boundary between solvent and insolvent is:
options: 1 : 1 — below it, debts exceed assets and continued trading carries legal consequences

questions.question: "Solvent but illiquid" describes a business that is:
options: Rich in cash with debts exceeding assets
Heavy with equipment yet unable to find Friday's wages — the whole game strong, the sprint failing
Failing both the acid test and the solvency test

questions.question: Solvency anchors the going concern assumption because:
options: Auditors invented the two terms together
Carrying assets at useful values presumes a future — a failing ratio shakes the foundation under the statements

subtopics.title: Return on Owner's Equity — Was It Worth It?

questions.question: Return on owner's equity divides by the AVERAGE equity because:
options: The equity moved during the year — profit flowing in, drawings flowing out — so the honest base is the mean of opening and closing
The formula summary prints it without a reason

questions.question: The calculation for Zanele's year is:
options: 10 500 / 25 000 × 100 = 42% — profit over the average of 22 000 and 28 000

questions.question: The return only gains meaning when compared against:
options: The safe alternative — a fixed deposit at about 7% — which the business must beat COMFORTABLY

questions.question: A business returning barely more than the bank's deposit rate is a warning because:
options: The profit figure must contain an error
The owner shoulders risk and does the work — a return matching the safe rate leaves that risk unpaid

questions.question: The format habit for analysis answers is:
options: Ratios AS ratios (4 : 1) and percentages as percentages — the format itself carries marks

questions.question: The classic dropped mark in return on equity is:
options: Using the UNAVERAGED equity — opening or closing alone — instead of the mean

questions.question: "Comments run both ways" in liquidity means:
options: Two formulas must always be quoted
Too LOW is dangerous (bills at risk) and too HIGH can mean idle resources — a mature answer can argue either

questions.question: Every ratio is best understood as:
options: A tradition kept for its own sake
A DECISION turned into a number — the bank deciding to lend, the owner deciding to stay, the supplier deciding to grant credit

questions.question: The month-end test asks:
options: Can what is coming in cover what is knocking at the door?
Did the year deliver a profit?
How old is the delivery vehicle?

questions.question: "I cannot pay the rent with tins of beans" is the household version of:
options: The acid test — re-asking the question with the hard-to-sell stock set aside

questions.question: R24 500 napping in the bank while the loan charges 10% shows:
options: Safety quietly turning into waste — keep enough ready, send the rest to work

questions.question: The whole-race count for the shop gives:
options: R55 600 owned against R27 600 owed — two rand for every rand owed: everyone could be paid

questions.question: The sprint and the whole race can disagree, for example when:
options: A family owns a fine house yet misses Friday's rent money — solvent, but illiquid
Profit grows in step with sales

questions.question: Trading while insolvent means:
options: Spending money that already belongs to the creditors — which is why the bank checks this number first

questions.question: The bank's order of questions is:
options: Could you pay AT ALL (solvency) before will you pay ON TIME (liquidity)

subtopics.title: Was It Worth the Owner's While?

questions.question: The owner's return works out to:
options: 42% — R10 500 earned on an average stake of R25 000

questions.question: The bank's 7% and the shop's 42% differ in nature because:
options: The 7% is PROMISED; the 42% was EARNED — with labour, stress and risk, and no promise of repeating
The shop's figure already includes the loan
Bank percentages use a different arithmetic

questions.question: A shop returning 8% against a safe 7% deserves the advice:
options: RETHINK — a year of work and full risk for one extra rand per hundred leaves the risk unpaid
Take out a second loan immediately

questions.question: This one ratio "joins the two statements" because:
options: It is printed on both pages
The formula summary lists it twice
Profit comes from the story page and the owner's stake from the photograph — one fraction answering a life decision
